crossOverSetup.title: Start with Graphics: Auto on CrossOver 26+
crossOverSetup.detail: Auto selects a backend using CrossOver's per-game database and falls back to Wine when there is no entry. This is our baseline for a trial, not a tested preset for this ETI package.

crossOverSetup.title: Use a dedicated bottle when changing settings
crossOverSetup.detail: Our recommendation is one bottle per game that needs custom settings. Explicit graphics selections affect every application in the bottle. Record the bottle's Windows version and any changes in your test notes.

crossOverSetup.title: Check dependencies against the actual package
crossOverSetup.detail: CrossTie recipes can install prerequisites and configure a bottle. A Steam or retail recipe may expect an installer that differs from ETI's synced files. Inspect the local package before choosing a recipe; automatic dependency setup is not available here yet.

crossOverSetup.title: Change one setting at a time
crossOverSetup.detail: During a trial, record graphics and MSync settings, then compare the same scene. CodeWeavers notes that MSync and High Resolution Mode do not benefit every application. Keep writable game settings and saves in the local installation.

nativeSetup.title: Prepare the Mac engine and game data
nativeSetup.detail: Use the port's own setup instructions, then select the installed Mac executable or app in Runtime. Keep writable settings outside the read-only Resilio package. A native runtime selection alone does not prove Windows LAN compatibility.

troubleshooting.title: Check the platform and date of a workaround
troubleshooting.detail: Confirm the exact game edition, macOS and CrossOver version before trying community advice. Historical Linux fixes and reports from Intel Macs are investigation leads, not Apple Silicon presets.

troubleshooting.title: Compare builds when LAN joining fails
troubleshooting.detail: For an ETI trial, record the game versions on both machines, package revision, maps and mods. ETI's package date is not the game's network protocol version. Test direct connection as well as lobby discovery where the game supports it.

lanChecklist: Record the Windows host's game version and the Mac client's version.
Join the Windows host and complete a match or level, then reconnect.
Repeat without WAN access after provisioning. Test Mac hosting separately.

profiles.summary: User-confirmed working LAN play with the Windows group on M2 Pro, macOS 15.7.9 and CrossOver 26.3.0. ETI package 20250308 contains v2024.11.26s (build 4936). The agent separately verified Skeld practice rendering and keyboard movement. The successful LAN result is user-reported; reconnecting, Mac hosting and operation without WAN remain untested.

setup.title: Match the participants' game versions
setup.detail: Use the same Windows package as the other ETI players and confirm the version shown in the game. The tested package reports v2024.11.26s, build 4936; a current store release may differ.

setup.title: Start with the tested clean bottle
setup.detail: The trial used a dedicated Windows 10 64-bit bottle, Graphics Auto, no additional dependencies and no launch arguments. Extract the synced amongus.eti into a writable local folder, select Among Us.exe and its containing folder in Runtime. UnRAR 7.23 extracted the tested package with CRC validation. The game reported Direct3D 11 and rendered The Skeld without a Warcraft-style OpenGL override.

troubleshooting.title: Steam account error versus Local play
troubleshooting.detail: This direct launch showed SteamworksAuthFail. After closing the message, Play → Local and Play → Practice remained usable in the tested build, and the user later confirmed LAN play worked. That does not establish online account functionality. Innersloth recommends launching through Steam for this sign-in error; do not treat it as a graphics failure or change DLLs to fix account authentication.

troubleshooting.title: Use a waiting lobby for discovery checks
troubleshooting.detail: The Local browser was initially empty when the other players had already started their round. The user subsequently confirmed successful LAN play with the Windows group. Repeat discovery checks with a known waiting lobby and matching builds. Tasks, discussion, voting and completed-round coverage were not individually recorded in that confirmation; record those details and reconnecting in future reports.

lanChecklist: Join a Windows-hosted Local lobby with the same game version.
Complete a round, including discussion and voting, then rejoin.
Repeat with WAN disconnected after provisioning; record account and chat requirements.

profiles.summary: This profile covers Left 4 Dead 2. Start with a dedicated CrossOver trial using the ETI Windows build; gameplay and co-op remain untested here.

setup.title: Keep this edition separate from Left 4 Dead 1
setup.detail: Check the installed game's version and content against the Windows host. Select the prepared local executable in Runtime and record any package-specific launch arguments.

troubleshooting.title: Old performance tips need revalidation
troubleshooting.detail: The linked tips are mostly from 2009–2010 and include Linux audio fixes. Do not treat old memory, GLSL or launch-argument tweaks as current M2 defaults. Start from the current CrossOver baseline.

lanChecklist: Join a Windows-hosted local co-op campaign with matching content.
Test input, sound, a level transition and reconnecting.
Repeat without WAN access after provisioning. Validate Mac hosting in a separate trial.

profiles.summary: Test the 2006 FlatOut 2 Windows package in CrossOver first. This is a different game from Ultimate Carnage; Mac-to-Windows LAN play is not yet verified.

setup.title: Keep the Windows build aligned
setup.detail: Prepare a local copy of the ETI package and record its actual game version. Treat a Mac release as a separate experiment until it can join the same Windows lobby.

troubleshooting.title: Change resolution in the separate graphics setup
troubleshooting.detail: Close the game. In Runtime, temporarily add -setup as an argument, save, then launch. In the configuration window, choose Display Mode with 32-bit colour and a matching Aspect Ratio, then click OK. Remove -setup from Runtime, save and launch normally. This was verified with ETI package 20160922 (game v1.2), CrossOver 26.3.0 and an M2 Pro on macOS 15.7.9.

troubleshooting.title: If the game stays in a small window
troubleshooting.detail: A low game resolution or a forced Wine virtual desktop can cause this. In the FlatOut 2 bottle, disable Emulate a virtual desktop if it was enabled, then reopen graphics setup and choose a supported screen resolution. Our local test reached the full-screen profile menu at 1512×945, 32-bit colour, 16:10, with Graphics Auto and High Resolution Mode off. Pick a mode suited to your own display; this startup check does not verify Windows LAN play.

troubleshooting.title: A missing DLL is a dependency clue
troubleshooting.detail: A 2009 tip mentions d3dx9_30.dll. If that exact error occurs, investigate the package's DirectX prerequisites and an official runtime installer. No individual DLL download or override has been validated for this profile.

troubleshooting.title: Skip Linux-only audio fixes on macOS
troubleshooting.detail: The historical tips include PulseAudio/ALSA advice, which is for Linux. It does not establish a macOS startup fix.

lanChecklist: Join the Windows ETI LAN lobby with matching builds.
Complete a race and a destruction derby; change tracks and reconnect.
Check input/controller behavior and repeat without WAN access after provisioning.

profiles.summary: Experimental target: a working CrossOver setup for this ETI package has not been established. Verify multiplayer startup before investing in a full setup recipe.

setup.title: Test the multiplayer executable explicitly
setup.detail: Identify the local multiplayer executable from the package and configure that entry for the LAN trial. Record single-player and multiplayer results separately if they behave differently.

troubleshooting.title: Intro-movie advice is historical
troubleshooting.detail: CodeWeavers lists a 2009 intro-movie hang workaround. It is not an M2-tested fix and should only be investigated if the observed failure matches. Read the current Mac compatibility reports before choosing further changes.

lanChecklist: Reach the multiplayer menu and record the actual game version.
Join a known Windows ETI server and complete a map, then reconnect.
Record input/audio issues and repeat without WAN access after provisioning.

profiles.summary: Classic Warcraft III 1.30.4.11274: local gameplay rendered correctly with -window and -opengl on an M2 Pro, macOS 15.7.9, CrossOver 26.3.0. Windows LAN joining was user-confirmed before the graphics fix; lobby discovery worked afterward. A complete LAN round with OpenGL remains untested.

setup.title: Prepare a writable local installation
setup.detail: Use a dedicated Windows 10 64-bit bottle, Graphics Auto, High Resolution Mode off and no forced virtual desktop. Our tested installation used C:\WarcraftIII\Warcraft III.exe, with C:\WarcraftIII as the working directory. Keep the synced distribution unchanged. UnRAR 7.23 extracted this package; macOS bsdtar and 7-Zip 26.03 could not extract its newer RAR dictionary correctly.

setup.title: Inspect the supplied setup helpers before replacing keys
setup.detail: The tested package included wc3_keys.exe and wc3_profile.exe as self-extracting archives. Inspect the setup script and archive destinations: the key helper targets C:\ProgramData\Blizzard Entertainment\Warcraft III; the profile helper targets Documents\Warcraft III. Use only license material you are entitled to use. Keep .w3k files and their contents private. The launcher does not execute these helpers automatically.

setup.title: Use the verified rendering arguments
setup.detail: In Runtime, add -window and -opengl as separate arguments. Save, then launch Warcraft III.exe. The built-in OpenGL renderer fixed black terrain and unit models in the local test. For full-screen play, use the macOS green window button after launching; -nativefullscr caused cropping in our setup.

setup.title: Select The Frozen Throne in the game
setup.detail: If Reign of Chaos opens, click the small portrait button immediately to the right of Single Player. It switches editions and restarts the game. Frozen Throne then persisted across launches. The package's -frozenthrone argument did not select the edition in this test.

troubleshooting.title: HUD and minimap work but the world is black
troubleshooting.detail: The menu alone did not reveal the rendering failure. Close the game and check that both -window and -opengl are saved. In our test, terrain, scenery, builder model, portrait and movement worked on the same custom map afterward. No extra graphics DLL or registry renderer override was needed.

troubleshooting.title: No LAN lobbies appear
troubleshooting.detail: Use the same game build, expansion and maps as the Windows host. A host must be waiting in a lobby; an already running classic match is not a join target. Accept the game's Bonjour installation prompt if shown, and check that Bonjour Service is running inside this game's bottle. Native macOS Bonjour alone does not confirm that Windows service is installed. Check local network permissions and firewall rules if needed; disabling the firewall is not part of this recipe.

troubleshooting.title: Some user files still go to Documents
troubleshooting.detail: CrossOver may map Windows Documents to your Mac Documents folder. Warcraft wrote a replay there despite a custom User Game Save Folder registry value. Back up Documents/Warcraft III too; do not assume all saves and replays are isolated inside the bottle.

lanChecklist: Confirm both clients show Frozen Throne and matching game versions; join a waiting Windows lobby.
With -window and -opengl, verify terrain, models and portraits, then complete a round.
Test map changes, reconnecting and Mac hosting separately. Repeat without WAN access after provisioning.

profiles.summary: Our first native-port experiment uses ioquake3's Universal 2 build. Apple Silicon engine availability is established; compatibility with the ETI Windows server still needs testing.

setup.title: Use the official Universal 2 build
setup.detail: Follow ioquake3's Mac download and player's guide to provide the required Quake III data. Then select the installed native executable or app in Runtime. The engine and game data are separate components.

setup.title: Record the server protocol, maps and mods
setup.detail: Compare the ETI Windows server's actual build with the selected engine. Begin with matching base-game content, then test the event's mods separately. No protocol override is applied by this guide.

troubleshooting.title: Keep native and CrossOver trials separate
troubleshooting.detail: These setup notes target ioquake3. If you switch Runtime to CrossOver, the saved choice is respected, but the native guide does not become a Windows recipe.

lanChecklist: Load the intended game data in the Apple Silicon engine.
Discover or directly connect to the Windows ETI host; complete a match.
Change maps, reconnect and test required mods. Repeat without WAN access after provisioning.
